**Emplois d'été Canada 2025: A Program to Support Young People**
The Emplois d'été Canada (EEC) program is part of the Stratégie emploi et compétences jeunesse (SECJ), a horizontal initiative of the Government of Canada implemented jointly by 12 federal ministries, organizations, and state-owned companies. The SECJ helps young people (15-30 years old), particularly those facing employment obstacles, to obtain employment support, skill-based training, and professional experience needed to integrate the labor market. The EEC program, administered by Emploi et Développement social Canada, provides salary subsidies to non-profit and public sector employers, as well as private sector organizations with 50 or fewer full-time employees, to offer quality summer jobs to young people aged 15-30. The funded jobs allow young people to improve their skills or acquire new ones. For many young people, it is their first work experience, which will influence their future education and career choices. The program takes into account national and local priorities, as well as labor market needs. Projects that support young people facing employment obstacles are prioritized, including those with disabilities, Indigenous youth, Black or 2ELGBTQI+ youth, and youth from racialized groups, rural or remote communities, or minority language communities. By offering young people equal opportunities to improve their skills, EEC facilitates their success in the labor market. The jobs funded by the EEC program are full-time (30-40 hours per week) and last 6-16 weeks, with an average of 8 weeks at 35 hours per week. The hiring period for young people for 2025 runs from April 21 to July 21, 2025, and the jobs will end no later than August 30, 2025. Up to 76,000 jobs counting for young people and our communities will be posted on the Government of Canada's Job Bank website and mobile app, which will be regularly updated. Young people can therefore frequently check the Job Bank to see which new jobs are offered in their community.
